settled: header is an operator: the iterable feeds into it
a real item port, wirable, never purely derived
zero-iterations arm always drawn and transparent

criteria.name: Tells the item cable apart from every other cable
Says the true fact — one per turn, not one turn late
Adds nothing the board has to carry twice
Survives two consumers, zip, and nesting
Stays a real port on a real cable you can drag

A.name: Dotted drop
A.one_line: Your drawing: the item falls from the header on a dotted line carrying `i =`.

B.name: Solid drop
B.one_line: The same run, drawn solid. The item is this turn's value, so it is ordinary data.

C.name: Source pill at the port
C.one_line: A source pill `other · Pose` right at the header, then an ordinary cable.

D.name: Cadence ticks
D.one_line: Solid, with a short cross-tick every few pixels: one tick, one turn.

E.name: Half-weight line
E.one_line: The item cable is drawn at half the weight of a data cable. Nothing else changes.

F.name: Ghost fan
F.one_line: The cable is solid, with two faded copies fanning behind it into the same port.

G.name: Named cap stub
G.one_line: A stub off the header ending in a labelled cap, and a matching cap at the consumer. No long cable.

H.name: Port above the consumer
H.one_line: The item port slides along the header to sit directly above the port it feeds.

I.name: Type on the port, name on the cable
I.one_line: The port says `Pose`; the cable says `other`. Your question, answered.

J.name: Operator row
J.one_line: `Iterable ▸ Iter` side by side on one header line: the header read as an operator with an in and an out.
